measurement.connection_metric: legacy unsafe_connections counts rejected proposed connections, excluded from emitted machine stitches
measurement.timing_scope: generate including interpretation, stitches, preview and machine export; excluding process startup and read-back audits

measurement.memory_scope: fresh worker process peak RSS including interpreter, libraries, generation and audits
measurement.coverage_meaning: coverage models top-layer thread width; structural_coverage adds 0.25 mm tolerance. Neither certifies coverage on fabric.
measurement.after_nonrepeated_load: final Python suite ran concurrently with part of the one-run corpus
measurement.after_repeated_load: three runs on straight, s-curve and taper after final Python suite; development UI remained available
measurement.beauty_and_real_relief: not measured; no foam/puff or machine sew-out validation

density_sensitivity.caveat: Increasing density can force another audited column decomposition. Falcon satin at 120% changes from 24 to 57 satin blocks and 30 to 66 trims; denser is not inherently better and does not create validated 3D relief.

limitations: A bounded corpus does not establish performance or quality on arbitrary logos, photographs or fabrics.
Serial worker timings exclude interpreter/import startup and machine read-back audits but include artwork interpretation, stitch generation, previews and exports.
Peak RSS includes the interpreter, native libraries, generation and audits; it is not isolated Python allocation memory.
One-run logo timings are observational and not stable performance medians. Three-run small-case medians remain shared-development measurements.
Running stitch is a contour rendition, not a full-coverage candidate, and is never recommended to replace a solid fill.
Legacy unsafe_connections counts proposed connections that were rejected, not unsafe emitted machine stitches.
Strict satin can still refuse unsuitable geometry; such refusals are retained instead of substituting tatami under a satin label.
Learning from screen preferences alone cannot establish fabric stability, needle safety or professional sewn appearance.
